Don't mind me. Just resting my feet a while, if that's alright.
I used to have a little cottage, you know. Two rooms and a vegetable patch.
Then one night a coal jumped out of the hearth and onto the thatch. Lost everything but the clothes on my back.
They chased me out of the last village. Hope you're a friendlier sort.
Said I was bad luck after their well ran dry. As if I'd drunk the whole thing myself!
Lovely place you've got. Not that I'd know much about having a place.
Some days the only thing I've got for company is my own stomach growling.
Rain last night, frost the night before. A roof would be a fine thing.
I'm no thief, I promise. Just down on my luck, is all.
Is it always this quiet here? Quiet's good. Quiet means nobody's shouting at me to move along.
Back home I was a cooper. Made the finest barrels in the valley, if I say so myself.
Then the brewery shut its doors, and nobody needed barrels any more. Funny how quick a trade can vanish.
